mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -32.9% to -26.7% over four weeks, indicating a consistent recovery trend. This sustained upward momentum will continue over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above its current baseline deficit.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 6.2 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has stabilized near -30.6% with minimal week-to-week volatility, indicating commuting patterns have plateaued. When TRANSIT remains flat for two consecutive weeks below -30%, retail recovery stalls because foot traffic from transit-dependent commuters does not increase.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains within ±2 percentage points of prior week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -30.6% in t-0w, -32.0% in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT stagnation, or TRANSIT rises above -28% in either of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen from 0.9% to 3.7% over four weeks, signaling increased essential-goods shopping. This behavioral shift toward essential errands crowds out discretionary retail visits. As GROCERY_PHARM continues rising, RETAIL_REC will decline because consumers consolidate trips and reduce non-essential spending.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 4% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 2.8 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases while GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 4%, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 2% within the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -23.3% to -13.4% over four weeks, indicating outdoor recreation is becoming a primary leisure activity. As PARKS mobility continues to improve, outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor retail-and-recreation venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 9.9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next four weeks, or PARKS falls below -15% in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained stable near -19% across four weeks with minimal recovery. When WORKPLACES fails to recover above -18% for two consecutive weeks, it signals remote work persistence. Persistent remote work reduces commuting-adjacent retail visits, capping RETAIL_REC recovery at current levels.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -18.5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -18.7% in t-0w, -19.0% in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises more than 4 percentage points over the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES stagnation, or WORKPLACES exceeds -17% in either of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 11.9% to 10.6% over four weeks, indicating people are spending less time at home and more time outside. This outbound shift, combined with TRANSIT stabilization below -30%, suggests capacity constraints or policy restrictions on indoor venues. RETAIL_REC will decline as indoor retail access remains constrained.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10.5% and TRANSIT remains below -30% in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points in the next week, or RESIDENTIAL rises above 11% while TRANSIT remains below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and RETAIL_REC show inverse momentum: PARKS improved 9.9 points while RETAIL_REC improved only 6.2 points over four weeks. This divergence indicates a substitution effect. If PARKS continues outpacing RETAIL_REC recovery, the substitution will intensify, causing RETAIL_REC to decline relative to baseline as outdoor recreation captures discretionary mobility.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves more than 2 percentage points faster than RETAIL_REC in any week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 9.9 points vs RETAIL_REC 6.2 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next four weeks, or PARKS falls below -15% in any week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both near -30% and -19% respectively with minimal recovery. When both remain flat for one week, it signals a locked-in remote-work equilibrium with low commuting. This equilibrium suppresses retail foot traffic within one week as the commuting-dependent customer base does not materialize.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES change by less than 1 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1 percentage point in the next week, or either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises by more than 2 percentage points.
